perturbed_solution: In $3\frac{1}{2}$ hours, Joann covers $\left(3\frac{1}{2}\text{ hours}\right)(11\text{ mph})=42$ miles.  If Fran's average speed in miles per hour is $s$, then Fran covers $3s$ miles in $3$ hours.  Solving $3s=42$ we find $s=\boxed{16}$ miles per hour.

errors.rationale: Incorrectly computed $3.5 \times 12$ as 40 instead of 42 by treating the fractional part imprecisely; student may have approximated $3 \times 12 + 0.5 \times 10 = 36 + 4 = 40$ or rounded prematurely.
Incorrectly added 3 to 42 and presented as the answer instead of dividing $42 \div 3 = 14$; the student performed $42 - 3 = 39$ or treated the equation as $s = 42 - 3 + 16$ instead of $s = 42 / 3$.

Misread or swapped Joann's speed from 12 mph to 11 mph; this is an error in the initial data entry that propagates and affects the distance computation, though the student still claims it equals 42 miles without recomputing.
